questions.question: In a certain code language, 'BRAVE' is written as '43' and 'BOTH' is written as '41'. How will 'ABACUS' be written in that code language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Sum of the place value - Number of letters in word.

Now,

'BRAVE' is written as '43'

⇒ B(2) + R(18) + A(1) + V(22) + E(5) = 48;

⇒ 48 - 5 = 43.

For, 'BOTH' is written as '41'

⇒ B(2) + O(15) + T(20) + H(8) = 45.

⇒ 45 - 4 = 41.

Similarly, for ‘ABACUS’

⇒ A(1) + B(2) + A(1) + C(3) + U(21) + S(19) = 47;

⇒** ****47 - 6 = 41.**

So, 'ABACUS' will be coded as '41'.

Hence, the correct answer is "41".

questions.question: Nine people, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, and I, are sitting in a row facing south. E sits in the middle. Three people sit between E and G. Six people sit between G and B. Three people sit between B and A. F sits second to the right of A. I sits fourth to the left of F. I and E are not immediate neighbours. B and C are not neighbours. H sits to the right of D. Who is sitting fourth to the right of G?
questions.solution:
Given: Nine people, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, and I. 

1) Six people sit between G and B.

2) Three people sit between E and G.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd18a95aff5c97e63990f419be7887b802ab496214d463aba07cd042425045d7.png] 

3) Three people sit between B and A.

4) F sits second to the right of A. 

5) I sits fourth to the left of F.

6) I and E are not immediate neighbors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6df1350ad3d65ceb8a2255eb0a76b405fc69c7977f05a7612421109223246f47.png] 

7) B and C are not neighbors. 

8) H sits to the right of D. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e963fd21f5eb91451a297095e546eae18fa4eacfebd2dc50e9e92c35fad44822.png] 

**So, we need to follow Case 1 because, according to the question, E sits in the middle.**

So, E is sitting fourth to the right of G.

Hence, the correct answer is **"E"**.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All cookies are sweet.

Some sweets are snacks.

**Conclusions:**

I. All sweets are cookies.

II. All cookies are snacks.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Statement:

All cookies are sweet.

Some sweets are snacks.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89edb9c42d66ed5792c81efff40f799a83b4a84368341b318db70c8e15108ae2.png] 

Conclusions:

(i) All sweets are cookies - False (Because All cookies are sweet, so All sweets are cookies can be possible not definite).

(ii) All cookies are snacks - False (There is no definite relation between Cookies and Snacks, so it is possible only).

Here, Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

I. No B is A.

II. No C is B.

**Conclusions:**

I. No C is A.

II. No A is B.

III. Some B are not C.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows
Both conclusions II and III follows

questions.solution:
Statement:

I. No B is A.

II. No C is B.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0135c14ec3a0a5a87111d2cd5e42bb39545f2f6b3395457a7e76f6eb94092fa5.png] 

Conclusions:

(i) No C is A - False (Because No definite relation given between C and A, so it can be possible only).

(ii) No A is B - True (No B is A, so no A is B also follow).

(iii) Some B are not C - True (No C is B, so Some B is not C)

Here, Both conclusions II and III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__****No C is B implies that Some C are not B or Some B are not C**.

questions.question: The height of five students, Aakriti, Kiran, Lisa, Manisha and Rekha, are compared. The height of Kiran is more than only two students. The height of Manisha is immediately greater than Rekha, and Rekha is immediately greater than Kiran. How many students are taller than Rekha?
questions.solution:
Given: Five students, Aakriti, Kiran, Lisa, Manisha and Rekha. 

The height of Kiran is more than only two students. 

__ > __ > Kiran > __ > __

The height of Manisha is immediately greater than Rekha, and Rekha is immediately greater than Kiran. 

Manisha > Rekha > Kiran > Kiran/Lisa > Lisa/Kiran

So, there are only one students are taller than Rekha.

Hence, the correct answer is **"One"**.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(3, 5, 30)

(6, 5, 60)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

(1st number **×** 2nd number **× 2)** = 3rd number.

Now,

(3, 5, 30)

⇒ (3 × 5 × 2) = 30.

For (6, 5, 60)

⇒ (6 × 5 × 2) = 60.

Now, checking the options:

Option 1: (4, 6, 38)

⇒ (4 × 6 × 2) = 48 ≠ 38.

**Option 2: (6, 7, 84) **

**⇒ (6 × 7 × 2) = 84 = 84.**

Option 3: (4, 7, 28)

⇒ (4 × 7 × 2) = 56 ≠ 28.

Option 4: (3, 9, 44)

⇒ (3 × 9 × 2) = 54 ≠ 44.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and also ‘–’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

1 × 14 + 30 – 20 ÷ 10 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation: 1 × 14 + 30 – 20 ÷ 10 = ?

Now, if** ****‘+’ and ‘×**‘ and **‘–’ and ‘÷’ ** are **interchanged**, then:

⇒ 1 + 14 × __**30 ÷ 20**__ - 10 = ?

⇒ 1 + __**14 **____**× 1.5**__ - 10 = ?

⇒ **__1 + 21__** - 10 = ?

⇒ __22 - 10__ = 12.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
